items.q: Are we losing the ability to have real conversations?
items.a: Johnson and Mycoskie **do not think so**. Their circles are swinging back toward dinner parties and vulnerability after a long digital stretch. Johnson's editor caveat: **WhatsApp can be real** for people not ready for eye-to-eye — a bridge, not a fake.

items.q: Where should a lonely man start if he cannot talk to other men?
items.a: Johnson: get honest **in the mirror** first so 'be more social' has a purpose. Mycoskie: **invite an old close friend to coffee** and ask about *their* life so they go first.

items.q: What did Blake's father regret, and what did Blake do?
items.a: Losing college and medical-school friends to family and work. At ~30 Blake emailed seven friends and started an **annual trip**. 19 years later the **Rugged Adventure Club** is 14 men — one of his biggest mental-health interventions.

items.q: What happened when Johnson tried to record his father's oral history?
items.a: He flew to Florida, bought gear, and his estranged father kept saying **we've got time**. Dad died. Johnson still has not written the obit. **Maintenance has a deadline.**

items.q: What did Mycoskie tell his kids after the two-year crisis?
items.a: He is **enough because he exists**, not because of TOMS or other people's opinions — and so are they. Dinner ritual: 'I am enough / you are enough / we are enough.' Unhealed not-enough had been **projecting performance pressure** onto his son.

items.q: What are the two depth tips they end on?
items.a: Johnson: **ask more questions than statements**, then **stand on them** ('Why not?' plus silence — they indict themselves). Mycoskie: **undistracted time** — leftover clock, sit in the pause, ask a clarifying follow-up before the next question.
